sections.content: Aurora, Colorado doesn't get as much buzz as its neighbor Denver, but savvy real estate investors have been quietly building wealth here for years. As the third-largest city in Colorado with over 390,000 residents, Aurora offers a rare combination of affordable entry points, strong population growth, and rising rents that make it a standout market in 2024 and beyond. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started — check out this guide to [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) if you're new to the game — finding real estate deals in Aurora CO is a strategy worth serious attention.
Aurora CO Real Estate Market Overview

Aurora sits at the eastern edge of the Denver metro and stretches across three counties: Arapahoe, Adams, and Douglas. The city has undergone significant transformation over the past decade, attracting major employers like Buckley Space Force Base, Children's Hospital Colorado, and the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. That kind of economic infrastructure drives consistent housing demand — which is exactly what investors need to see before committing capital to a market.

As of mid-2024, the median home price in Aurora sits around $450,000, though you'll find plenty of properties in the $300,000–$380,000 range in older neighborhoods on the north and east sides of the city. This is notably lower than Denver's median, which hovers near $550,000, giving Aurora a competitive edge for investors who need room to make the numbers work. Days on market have been running between 25 and 40 days for move-in-ready homes, while distressed or dated properties can sit longer — creating opportunity for buyers who know what to look for.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Aurora

Not all of Aurora is created equal from an investment standpoint. The city spans nearly 160 square miles, so location matters enormously when you're evaluating deals. Here's a breakdown of the neighborhoods that consistently attract investor interest.
North Aurora (Montview and Lyn Knoll Areas)

North Aurora is the classic value-add zone. Homes here were built primarily in the 1960s and 1970s, which means lots of dated kitchens, original bathrooms, and deferred maintenance — all signs of potential wholesale or flip opportunity. Entry prices in this area frequently fall in the $290,000–$340,000 range, with after-repair values (ARVs) often landing between $400,000 and $430,000 after a solid cosmetic renovation. Run your numbers carefully using a free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) before making any offer.
The Fitzsimons Corridor

The area surrounding the Anschutz Medical Campus has seen explosive growth. Medical professionals and university staff create a steady pool of renters and buyers, which keeps vacancy rates low. Investors targeting buy-and-hold rentals love this corridor because turnover is minimal and tenants tend to be higher income. Expect to pay more here — median prices run $480,000 to $520,000 — but cap rates can still pencil at around 5% to 6% if you source deals below market.
Southlands and Southeast Aurora

Southeast Aurora is a newer, more suburban feel with homes built from the 1990s through the 2010s. This zone attracts families and professionals priced out of the Denver Tech Corridor. It's a strong market for buy-and-hold investors looking for turnkey or light-rehab rentals. The Southlands Mall area anchors a strong retail and dining scene that keeps the neighborhood desirable. Prices here run $480,000 to $580,000, so your margins are tighter — but so is your risk.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Aurora
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in Aurora, particularly in north and central Aurora where older housing stock creates motivated seller scenarios. Estate sales, tired landlords, and pre-foreclosures are common deal sources. If you're new to this strategy, the guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) is worth reading before you start making offers. Assignment fees in Aurora typically run $10,000 to $25,000 depending on the deal, with higher fees possible on larger value-add plays.
Fix and Flip

Aurora's older housing inventory creates a healthy pipeline for fix-and-flip investors. A typical north Aurora flip might look like this: purchase at $310,000, invest $55,000 in renovations (new kitchen, two bathrooms, paint, flooring, landscaping), and sell at $415,000. After holding costs and agent fees, a disciplined investor might net $25,000 to $35,000. That math only works if you buy right — which means finding off-market or distressed listings before they hit the MLS. Learn how in this detailed guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).
Rental Properties

Aurora's rental market is strong and getting stronger. Average rents for a 3-bedroom single-family home run $2,100 to $2,600 per month depending on location and condition. With Aurora's population expected to keep growing as Denver becomes less affordable, demand for rentals isn't going anywhere. Multi-family properties — duplexes and small apartment buildings — are harder to find but command strong interest when they hit the market. If you're building a rental portfolio, Aurora deserves a serious look.

Before you commit to any deal in Aurora, use the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to stress-test your numbers. Plug in your purchase price, estimated rehab, ARV, and holding costs to see if the deal truly pencils — and at what price point it stops making sense. This 60-second check can save you from a very expensive mistake.
Aurora CO Market Trends to Watch in 2024–2025

items: Population growth continues: Aurora added over 15,000 residents between 2020 and 2023, and projections show no slowdown through 2030.
Interest rate sensitivity: Higher rates have cooled retail buyer demand, which means motivated sellers are more motivated — good news for investors with cash or hard money.
Rent growth is stabilizing: After years of rapid rent increases, Aurora's rental market is seeing more moderate 3–5% annual growth, which still beats inflation.
New construction is limited in north Aurora: Older neighborhoods can't easily add new supply, which protects ARVs and resale values for flippers.
Transit expansion: The RTD light rail network connecting Aurora to downtown Denver continues to boost demand near station areas, especially along the I-225 corridor.
Institutional buyers are active: Large investors and iBuyers have pulled back slightly from Denver suburbs, opening more opportunity for individual investors and small funds.

sections.content: Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Aurora

Aurora is absolutely investable from out of state — thousands of investors do it successfully — but you need to approach it with a solid local infrastructure. Here's how to get started on the right foot.

items: Build your local team first: Find a property manager before you close your first deal. Look for PM companies with experience in Aurora specifically, not just the broader Denver metro.

Use an investor-friendly agent: A general real estate agent won't have the off-market connections or investor mindset you need. Ask agents directly how many investment properties they've helped close in Aurora in the past 12 months.
Drive the market virtually: Google Street View is your friend for neighborhood assessment, but also tap into local Facebook groups, neighborhood apps like Nextdoor, and city crime map data.

Understand Colorado landlord-tenant law: Colorado is generally considered a landlord-friendly state, but there are nuances around security deposits, notice requirements, and eviction timelines. Know these before you buy.

Get pre-qualified for hard money or DSCR loans: Many Aurora deals — especially wholesales and flips — move fast. Having financing lined up in advance puts you in a position to act when the right deal appears.

Analyze before you fall in love with a deal: Use a structured analysis framework like the one outlined in [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) to keep emotions out of your decision-making.

sections.content: The best real estate markets aren't always the ones making headlines. The cities right next door — with stronger fundamentals and lower prices — are often where the real money gets made. Aurora is exactly that kind of market.

If you're ready to start sourcing deals in the Aurora market, the most important thing you can do right now is build your pipeline. That means direct mail to absentee owners, driving for dollars (even virtually), building relationships with local wholesalers, and monitoring probate and pre-foreclosure filings through Arapahoe and Adams County records.
